author: Bobby Grayson
description:
Two pre-existing check.sh facts a sibling or the integrator will hit, neither introduced by this piece.

(1) On a cold worktree the first ./check.sh reports 36/37 fixtures, failing maps with "object file .lake/build/lib/lean/Leanactors/AssocList.olean of module Leanactors.AssocList does not exist". The '== translator fixtures' stage runs before '== prove', and a fixture marked '# lean: check' compiles generated Lean against the built library, which does not exist until lake build has run once. The second ./check.sh in the same worktree is green (37/37). Either move the fixture stage after lake build, or have run_fixtures.exs build the library first.

(2) 'elixir elixir/test/run_fixtures.exs | grep -v "^PASS "' takes grep's exit status, so under set -e a fixture failure does not stop the run; the FAIL line only shows in the output. The new readiness stage avoids this by writing to a file and grepping the file, so --strict's exit code still reaches set -e.
title: check.sh: the fixture stage needs the oleans, and its exit status is swallowed
